newsitem.title: ECUADOR: U.S. may adopt trade sanctions vs Ecuador - paper. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 17/5]
newsitem.headline: U.S. may adopt trade sanctions vs Ecuador - paper. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 17/5]

text.p: The United States may clamp trade sanctions on Ecuador for allegedly violating copyright protection agreements, a U.S. embassy official in Quito said in comments published Friday.
"Ecuador has been alerted," El Telegrafo newspaper quoted U.S. trade attache Michael Glover as saying.
Glover said that in September this year the U.S. Trade Representative will review the situations of countries with which it has intellectual property accords.
"If Ecuador has not resolved these issues, there will be an evaluation and if it is necessary, further action will be taken," he said.

This could include making Ecuador one of Washington's Priority Foreign Countries "which will mean an investigation to determine whether its policies and practices merit the imposition of commercial sanctions," said Glover. (Corrects from "Priority Watch List" to "Priority Foreign Countries").
The United States is the top foreign sales destination for Ecuador's exports, including seafood, bananas and flowers.
Washington has been running out of patience after four years of delays in Ecuador's Congress in approving a bilateral accord on intellectual property protection.
Glover said Ecuador was "losing opportunities to attract foreign investment because of inadequate policies" -- investment it can ill afford to lose, said the U.S. diplomat.

"The flow of capital to all of South America has grown by 25 percent. In Peru, the rise was 104 percent, in Argentina 49 percent, in Bolivia 14 percent, but in Ecuador it has fallen 32 percent," he said.
